top_reviews.title: Amazing boots
top_reviews.text:
I've never owned a serious pair of leather boots before, thinking them too heavy and uncomfortably warm/hot. I've always worn hiking shoes or synthetic boots - and still use them. But these boots have changed my mind. They are great backpacking boots that can also be used for hiking. They are comfortable, light and not any warmer than my synthetic boots. 9 months later, I want to add something to my review. I hike in the winter and have some winter hiking boots for snowy hikes when my boots will get very wet. I’m a size 13 and they fit and feel perfect from the very first day. This is actually my third pair. I wear them year round. Not too hot in summer and not too cold in winter with some good socks. top_reviews.title: Terrible ever since they moved moved the plant to Mexico
top_reviews.text:
Updated below.

I have been wearing Justin 3133s almost daily for over 30 years. First to school and on the ranch as a work boot, and then as a uniform boot. When I first buy them, I write the date in them, and then I would write the date in them every time I had a new sole put on them. Well that was back when they were worth having repaired. Today they're like most everything else. The quality is out the window and you throw them away. The proof is that I still have 3133 Ropers that are dated from high school in the 80s. Ever since they moved the operation to Mexico, the stitching blows out LONG before the soles wear through, and then if you try to get them repaired the leather won't hold, plus they have to get deeper bite which makes them fit tighter than before. In Justin's ultimate wisdom they now have what they CALL a Roper that is American made, but it's not the 3133. It's a different leather that doesn't shine up well for a uniform boot, they fit differently so you'll likely wear a different size, and it has a contrasting color stitching around the top. The two stars is for Justin's commitment to quality. If you need a plain black cowboy boot that is pretty comfortable just buy them, put a little liquid nails on them when they start blowing apart, and then toss them and go buy another pair.

Hey Justin: How about bringing the original 3133 back to America to be made, and send that two bit imitation Roper down there?

Update: I changed my rating from two stars to one star as they have gotten even worse. I really planned to do my first ever video review, but it seems I never have the time.

As I stated above, I write the date in my boots the first time I wear them. I didn't start wearing these until the end of March 2014, and these were just going to be a pair of non-work boots that I just kept nice and wore to the office. Additionally, that means that I don't wear these everyday. Then a few weeks ago at the end of December 2014, I was walking in on a rainy day and notice my foot was wet. I looked down and the stitching had already blown out on the inside of one of the boots. Then a week or so later I noticed it had blown out on the other boot as well.

It's also important to note that these boots have never even needed to be polished! They've been worn occasionally to the office, for 9 months, and have been so lightly worn that they're not even scuffed. The soles still have plenty of leather on them, yet the stitching has blown out.

After almost 4 decades I'm abandoning Justin and have purchased a pair of Lucchese Ropers. They look essentially the same as the Justin 3133s and cost more at the time of purchase, but they're MADE IN THE U.S.A. and from what others have told me they'll last me many times longer than the Justins. Therefor over the long haul perhaps I'll actually save money.

top_reviews.title: Can’t walk a mile in my boots
top_reviews.text: These are the best cowboy boots I’ve ever worn, hell, not even sneakers beat these. These black ropers tell a story of a time when men were men. These days, we number in few. They’re even better when they become worn and lose the shine. Boots are made to get dirt on them and kicking ass. I work in the warehouse all night, and laze about at the local motorcycle shop all day long. I can wear them all doggone day with no fuss. The old west lives on with every step I take. I ride my Harley in them, I know I’m short and these boots are small, but you wouldn’t be able to walk a mile in my boots. These are ass kickers are mine, and I’m a proud owner. A little advice, go one size smaller then what you wear regularly.

Also, I ordered EE width and as another reviewer noted, the EEE is better for a genuinely wide foot. I cringe at what a D width would feel like if you didn't have a narrow foot!

top_reviews.title: amazon buyers beware
top_reviews.text:
Over the years I've owned several pairs of Allen Edmonds shoes, each of which I've purchased from my local menswear retailer and each of which bears the brand's extraordinary craftsmanship and attention to detail. I expected no less from the pair of AE McAllisters that I recently purchased from Amazon, and I was amazed by the fast turn-around--I ordered them on a Sunday night and by Tuesday afternoon they were at my door.

Yet the shoes that Amazon sent were appallingly disappointing: not only were they the wrong size (a 12 rather than the 11 that I ordered), and not only did they have a rubber sole and heel (rather than the oak leather sole and custom heel that's on every other pair of McAllisters I've ever owned or seen), but they were clearly, unmistakably USED: the vamp was deeply creased at the instep; the heel pocket leather was glossy and dark with wear; the laces were kinked and frayed; the sole was worn; the toes were badly scuffed, and there was a thin veneer of crud all along the welt. Even with a cursory glance, one could tell that someone else had worn the shoes for some time before sending them back. And then Amazon turned around and sold them to me as new.

The thing, though, is this: I'm not the only one who has received AE shoes like this from Amazon. Shortly after I received my shoes, I came across a thread on one of the better-known menswear internet discussion boards in which a number of AE customers registered strikingly similar complaints. I returned the shoes to Amazon, but who knows? You might be the one who gets them next.

In short, I will continue to buy Allen Edmonds shoes, but not from Amazon. Caveat emptor!

top_reviews.title: Not the quality I expected
top_reviews.text: I think the quality has dropped since I purchased my previous pair in the late 1990's.  That pair lasted me for years.  I've had this pair for just over a year and I don't wear them daily.  Not even weekly.  The left sole already has a hole in it and the stitching that holds the sole to the upper is coming undone.  I was reading the AE wikipedia page and it looks like they were sold in 2006 and then ownership transferred again in 2013.  Some of the production has been moved to the Dominican Republic and then the parts are shipped back to the US so it can be considered "Made in the USA".  Maybe they just don't have the quality they used to, but I would not recommend this as a durable reliable shoe anymore.  This is especially disappointing since I grew up near their headquarters and worked in the factory a couple of summers.  I feel old saying this but I guess, “they just don’t make ‘em like they used to.”

top_reviews.title: Terrible ever since they moved moved the plant to Mexico
top_reviews.text:
Updated below.

I have been wearing Justin 3133s almost daily for over 30 years. First to school and on the ranch as a work boot, and then as a uniform boot. When I first buy them, I write the date in them, and then I would write the date in them every time I had a new sole put on them. Well that was back when they were worth having repaired. Today they're like most everything else. The quality is out the window and you throw them away. The proof is that I still have 3133 Ropers that are dated from high school in the 80s. Ever since they moved the operation to Mexico, the stitching blows out LONG before the soles wear through, and then if you try to get them repaired the leather won't hold, plus they have to get deeper bite which makes them fit tighter than before. In Justin's ultimate wisdom they now have what they CALL a Roper that is American made, but it's not the 3133. It's a different leather that doesn't shine up well for a uniform boot, they fit differently so you'll likely wear a different size, and it has a contrasting color stitching around the top. The two stars is for Justin's commitment to quality. If you need a plain black cowboy boot that is pretty comfortable just buy them, put a little liquid nails on them when they start blowing apart, and then toss them and go buy another pair.

Hey Justin: How about bringing the original 3133 back to America to be made, and send that two bit imitation Roper down there?

Update: I changed my rating from two stars to one star as they have gotten even worse. I really planned to do my first ever video review, but it seems I never have the time.

As I stated above, I write the date in my boots the first time I wear them. I didn't start wearing these until the end of March 2014, and these were just going to be a pair of non-work boots that I just kept nice and wore to the office. Additionally, that means that I don't wear these everyday. Then a few weeks ago at the end of December 2014, I was walking in on a rainy day and notice my foot was wet. I looked down and the stitching had already blown out on the inside of one of the boots. Then a week or so later I noticed it had blown out on the other boot as well.

It's also important to note that these boots have never even needed to be polished! They've been worn occasionally to the office, for 9 months, and have been so lightly worn that they're not even scuffed. The soles still have plenty of leather on them, yet the stitching has blown out.

After almost 4 decades I'm abandoning Justin and have purchased a pair of Lucchese Ropers. They look essentially the same as the Justin 3133s and cost more at the time of purchase, but they're MADE IN THE U.S.A. and from what others have told me they'll last me many times longer than the Justins. Therefor over the long haul perhaps I'll actually save money.

I work in the warehouse all night, and laze about at the local motorcycle shop all day long. I can wear them all doggone day with no fuss. The old west lives on with every step I take. I ride my Harley in them, I know I’m short and these boots are small, but you wouldn’t be able to walk a mile in my boots. These are ass kickers are mine, and I’m a proud owner. A little advice, go one size smaller then what you wear regularly.

I expected no less from the pair of AE McAllisters that I recently purchased from Amazon, and I was amazed by the fast turn-around--I ordered them on a Sunday night and by Tuesday afternoon they were at my door.

Yet the shoes that Amazon sent were appallingly disappointing: not only were they the wrong size (a 12 rather than the 11 that I ordered), and not only did they have a rubber sole and heel (rather than the oak leather sole and custom heel that's on every other pair of McAllisters I've ever owned or seen), but they were clearly, unmistakably USED: the vamp was deeply creased at the instep; the heel pocket leather was glossy and dark with wear; the laces were kinked and frayed; the sole was worn; the toes were badly scuffed, and there was a thin veneer of crud all along the welt. Even with a cursory glance, one could tell that someone else had worn the shoes for some time before sending them back. And then Amazon turned around and sold them to me as new.

The thing, though, is this: I'm not the only one who has received AE shoes like this from Amazon. Shortly after I received my shoes, I came across a thread on one of the better-known menswear internet discussion boards in which a number of AE customers registered strikingly similar complaints. I returned the shoes to Amazon, but who knows? You might be the one who gets them next.

In short, I will continue to buy Allen Edmonds shoes, but not from Amazon. Caveat emptor!

top_reviews.title: Not the quality I expected
top_reviews.text: I think the quality has dropped since I purchased my previous pair in the late 1990's.  That pair lasted me for years.  I've had this pair for just over a year and I don't wear them daily.  Not even weekly.  The left sole already has a hole in it and the stitching that holds the sole to the upper is coming undone.  I was reading the AE wikipedia page and it looks like they were sold in 2006 and then ownership transferred again in 2013.  Some of the production has been moved to the Dominican Republic and then the parts are shipped back to the US so it can be considered "Made in the USA".  Maybe they just don't have the quality they used to, but I would not recommend this as a durable reliable shoe anymore.  This is especially disappointing since I grew up near their headquarters and worked in the factory a couple of summers.  I feel old saying this but I guess, “they just don’t make ‘em like they used to.”
